title: Microsoft Teams: pop out the sign language interpreter video in meetings
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned rollout, user steps and absence of an admin policy. Minor corrections should acknowledge differing Microsoft guidance on the IP video setting and cite the documentation for policy assignment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The accessibility guide does not tie guest access to the interpreter pop-out.
claims.quote: Searched: "sign language" "pop" "policy" Teams; Teams "pop out interpreters". Read the full accessibility guide: it describes guest access and interpreter video feeds but does not mention the interpreter pop-out.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The accessibility guide ties the IP video meeting policy setting to interpreters sharing an IP video feed.
claims.quote: Give sign language interpreters the ability to share IP video feed during Microsoft Teams meetings ... Check that IP video is turned On
claims.fix: Keep the attribution to the accessibility guide, and add: 'The audio and video policy article currently warns that Video conferencing does not turn off video for meetings and events, and directs organisers to Allow camera for attendees in Meeting Options.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-audio-and-video. This is differing general video-control guidance, not documentation of a pop-out switch.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The accessibility guide gives Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Audio & video > IP video.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Meetings, and then select Meeting policies. ... Select the policy you want to modify. ... Go to the Audio & video section. ... Check that IP video is turned On
claims.fix: Keep the cited path, but add: 'For the Unified Policies & Settings management experience, the accessibility guide says these options are under Settings & Policies. The audio and video policy article calls IP video "Video conferencing".' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-audio-and-video alongside the existing accessibility guide.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowIPVideo $true to allow sharing video.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module. ... -AllowIPVideo ... Set this to TRUE to allow the user to share their video. ... -Identity ... Specify the name of the policy being created.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether the interpreter pop-out depends on or is governed by IP video.
claims.quote: Searched: "sign language" "pop" "policy" Teams; Teams sign language interpreter pop out admin policy PowerShell AllowIPVideo roles licence price. Read accessibility guide, audio/video policies, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and MC1559642; none ties IP video specifically to the pop-out.

claims.where: controls[1].scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Meeting policies are assigned to users and the IP video setting applies to policy holders.
claims.quote: You can assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment (if supported for the policy type), or to a group that the users are members of (if supported for the policy type).
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-overview to sources for the existing statement that meeting policies are assigned to users. Keep the statement and the user scope.
